text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:

- Germany's leading health insurance companies will raise their fees from December 1. Insurers say unexpected increases in obligations. But rate increase likely to be valid only for December because rates will be cut again in January.

- New German shop opening laws take effect from today. Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt expects higher retail sales as a result. About 75 percent of the retailers plan to keep shopes open longer. They now allowed to keep their doors open until 8 p.m. during the week and 4 p.m. on Saturdays.
- The number of abortions in Germany rises in first quarter to 33,500, 8,900 more than a year earlier.
- Unknown assailants attack main office of Mercedes-Benz in Berlin. Nine windows broken and firebombs thrown inside.
- Optimism that Euro will be in place by 1999 spreads in Germany. Despite budget problems in France and Germany, more and more financial experts expect punctual start for EMU.
- German companies need to strengthen their profiles in Asia, says chairman of Siemens Heinrich von Pierer at Asian-Pacific conference in New Delhi.
- Dresdner Bank profits reach record levels after first nine months.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl to meet Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto today in Tokyo
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to make further cuts in Defence and Transport Ministry budgets
- Crime in Germany declines in 1995 for the first time since 1980.
- About 3,000 students, parents and teachers protest closing of school in Berlin
